model.reason: Qwen3-30B-A3B expert SHAPES (C=2048, H=768), synthetic weights; no model executed

headline: The §3 corpus closed last block with every primitive verified ALONE. This campaign's own law says LOCAL ADEQUACY DOES NOT COMPOSE -- stated about representations and equally open about KERNELS. Composing five of them into one graph found TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECTS, both of the same kind: A LAUNCH THAT NEVER ASKED THE KERNEL WHAT IT NEEDED. One was mine this block; the other had been shipped for many blocks and REFUTES A PUBLISHED CLAIM.

DEFECT_1_the_graph_could_not_hold_its_ow.what_the_graph_receipt_claimed: RUNTIME.graphs moved LARGE -> PARTIAL and the runtime was said to give 'most of the ORDERING/BATCHING value'. Every number in that receipt came from ELEMENTWISE nodes.
DEFECT_1_the_graph_could_not_hold_its_ow.the_defect: AirGraphNode carried only an element count and a scalar threadgroup, so the executor DERIVED a 1-D grid of blocks*threadgroup and an output of shape (n,). A row-wise norm needs grid = rows*threadgroup and (rows, cols); a tiled matmul needs a 3-D grid, a (tile, tile) threadgroup, parameters named A and B and an output named C. NONE of AIR's real primitives fit.

AND_IT_FAILED_IN_THE_WORST_WAY_-_IT_SOME.reading: SAME DEFECT, OPPOSITE APPEARANCES. Where the derived block count EXCEEDS the row count the extra threadgroups run OUT OF BOUNDS and the answer still looks right; where it FALLS SHORT rows are never computed and the answer is visibly wrong. A graph that holds a row-wise kernel is correct BY ACCIDENT OF SHAPE.

DEFECT_1_the_graph_could_not_hold_its_ow.reading: SAME DEFECT, OPPOSITE APPEARANCES. At 8x1024 the graph launched 32 threadgroups where the norm needed 8 -- 24 ran OUT OF BOUNDS on both buffers -- AND THE ANSWER MATCHED THE ORACLE TO 2.6e-07. At 8x64 it launched 2 for 8 rows and was wrong by 2.62; at 64x128, 32 for 64 rows, wrong by 5.21. An out-of-bounds access that happens to be benign is the same class as a race that does not fire: correct BY ACCIDENT OF SHAPE.
DEFECT_1_the_graph_could_not_hold_its_ow.fix: grid, threadgroup, output shape, parameter names and output name are now FIELDS, and node_for() fills them from the op's own launch() and out_shape(). THE GEOMETRY COMES FROM THE OP, NOT FROM A GUESS -- the same principle as the HUMF block's 'the plan names its source', arrived at independently.

DEFECT_2_a_published_claim_refuted_by_it.the_claim: ACCELERATOR_SIMDGROUP_GEMM.json justified keeping the tiled strategy in its own words: 'simdgroup ... REQUIRES every dimension to be a multiple of 8 and REFUSES otherwise ... while TILED HAS NO SHAPE CONSTRAINT -- deleting tiled would have removed the only strategy that handles a 60x60 matmul.'
DEFECT_2_a_published_claim_refuted_by_it.verdict: REFUTED BY THE EXAMPLE IT CITED. 60x60x60 on the tiled strategy was WRONG BY 3.84. 8x64x32 wrong by 4.65, 17x64x32 by 5.84. Every wrong case has m NOT a multiple of the tile and every right case has m a multiple -- n and k do not matter, and 48x80x32 with k=80 is fine.
DEFECT_2_a_published_claim_refuted_by_it.where_the_bug_was_NOT: the kernel body is FULLY GUARDED -- it checks gy < m, gx < n and k0 + lx < k -- so the tile was never the constraint and the kernel could always handle any shape
DEFECT_2_a_published_claim_refuted_by_it.where_it_was: launch() returned (n, m, 1) against a (tile, tile) threadgroup, which UNDER-DISPATCHES whenever m is not a multiple of the tile. One line: round both grid dimensions up to whole threadgroups. All 7 cases correct after, including the 60x60x60.
DEFECT_2_a_published_claim_refuted_by_it.why_it_survived: every GEMM receipt in this program measured square multiples of 16 -- 512, 1024, 2048, 4096 -- so the grid was always already a multiple of the tile and the defect could not appear. The claim about odd shapes was never TESTED at an odd shape.
DEFECT_2_a_published_claim_refuted_by_it.how_it_was_found: not by auditing the matmul. The composed block was wrong at T=8 and right at T=64 and T=96, and T=8 is the only one where m < tile.

the_composition_itself.block: y = x + W_down @ silu(W_gate @ rmsnorm(x)) -- the gated MLP that follows attention in all four specimens, at Qwen3-30B-A3B expert shapes C=2048 H=768
the_composition_itself.what_composition_bought: two defects that ALL the per-primitive checks passed over. The kernels were right; the way they were LAUNCHED was not, and a launch is exactly the thing a single-primitive test never varies because it uses the op's own execute().

one_submission_against_one_per_node.verdict: PREDICTED 1.5-3.0x and SHRINKING WITH T. Measured 2.216x at T=8, 2.035x at T=64 -- both inside the band -- and 1.415x at T=512, BELOW the band. The SHRINK was predicted and is confirmed; the magnitude at the largest size MISSED LOW, which is the first miss in that direction after six consecutive misses HIGH, and it is reported rather than the band widened.
one_submission_against_one_per_node.why_the_shrink: four extra submissions cost a fixed ~0.16-0.25 ms each; at T=512 the real GPU work is 1.77 ms, so the same fixed saving is a smaller fraction. The FIFTH sighting of the submission floor, and the first on a COMPOSITE rather than a single primitive.
one_submission_against_one_per_node.noise_stated: the T=64 graph arm carries 19.41% IQR and is admitted by a 5.3x margin-over-noise rather than a clean gate; T=8 and T=512 are clean

claim_boundary.not_a_transformer_block: no attention, no KV cache, no rotary, no residual stream across layers -- this is the MLP half of one block
claim_boundary.eager_is_the_control_not_a_mode: the per-node arm exists only to give the batched number a baseline; nobody would run a graph that way
claim_boundary.the_graph_still_serialises: serial_depth is 5 of 5 nodes, so this measures ORDERING and BATCHING and says NOTHING about concurrency -- the same split the AirGraph receipt insisted on
